name: Bilateral Renal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Bilateral Renal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Ultrasound or MRI showing bilateral multicystic, non-functioning kidneys with absence of normal renal parenchyma
Evidence of severe renal insufficiency or failure in neonatal period
Histological confirmation of immature, disorganized renal tissue with cyst formation if biopsy performed
Exclusion of other causes of cystic kidney disease such as polycystic kidney disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral multicystic kidneys on imaging plus clinical evidence of renal insufficiency in neonatal period
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not definitive; biopsy rarely performed due to clinical risks.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral renal hypoplasia with multicystic dysplastic kidneys
searchTerms: small kidneys with multiple cysts on both sides
bilateral renal hypoplasia with cystic malformation
very low or no urine output in newborn
newborn with little or no urine
high blood pressure due to kidney failure

common.symptomName: Poor feeding and failure to thrive in neonate
searchTerms: poor feeding and growth in infant
feeding difficulties and poor weight gain

common.symptomName: Polyuria in surviving infants with partial function
searchTerms: excessive urination in infants with partial kidney function
underdeveloped lungs due to low amniotic fluid
anemia caused by chronic kidney disease
low red blood cells from kidney failure

rare.symptomName: Congenital anomalies of the urinary tract (e.g., vesicoureteral reflux)
Neurological complications due to uremic encephalopathy
searchTerms: brain problems from kidney failure toxins
neurological symptoms due to kidney failure

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal failure
Electrolyte disturbances including hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis
Anemia consistent with chronic kidney disease
imaging: Ultrasound showing bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys with absent normal renal architecture
MRI confirming cystic renal dysplasia and absence of functional renal tissue
Chest X-ray may show pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to oligohydramnios
other: Histopathology (if biopsy performed) showing immature, disorganized renal tissue with cyst formation

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse cystic dilation of collecting ducts rather than dysplastic cysts
Usually presents with enlarged kidneys rather than hypoplastic kidneys
Bilateral enlarged kidneys with numerous cysts
Family history positive in most cases
Complete absence of one or both kidneys rather than dysplastic cystic kidneys
Often associated with other congenital anomalies

redFlags: Neonatal anuria or oliguria indicating severe renal failure
Severe electrolyte imbalances (e.g., hyperkalemia) risking cardiac arrhythmias
Pulmonary hypoplasia due to oligohydramnios causing respiratory distress
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD): Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney
UpToDate: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract
